original_summary: Growl is a 4-10 player hidden-team card game. Cards from a shared face-up deck are handed to other players, and on Night phases each player silently passes one card left and one right. Wounds kill a player, and bites secretly turn humans into werewolves. Humans win if at least one human survives the Final Night.

review.evidence: In the original, whoever sits next to a wolf receives its bites, so seat adjacency decides much of who gets infected. In the previous variation, a thoughtless wolf policy won about 70% at 6 players: bloc-vote one human and focus both Mauls on one target (or focus Bites for a hidden infection swing). A round-6 timeout also handed the win to any surviving wolf. Balance swung from about 70/30 at 6 players to about 45/55 at 7.

The previous variation's human win rate moved from about 0.15 to about 0.65 depending on one random exposure draw. The day-1 lynch and Salve choices were blind guesses. A strong human reasoner was not clearly better than a random voter.

Wolves had real decisions (Maul, Bite or a disguising Salve). Humans had almost no reliable signal: Charm feedback could clear a human but never identify a wolf. So the human side had little room to improve.
Hidden roles give plenty to infer, but the only hard evidence of a wolf was a random 2/N exposure each night. Vote patterns helped only a little.
Deaths, infections and team victory all follow from counters and comparisons.

The original uses seat adjacency (pass left and right), a seeded deck and hands. The previous variation fit the step limits but hid five kinds of information: roles, bites, night actions, the den, and private Charm feedback. The limit is 3. Some edge cases were also unstated: Mauling a wolf, when a new wolf joins the den, and the order of death versus infection.

problems: P1: The wolf bloc-vote plus focus-Maul or focus-Bite policy wins about 70% at 6 players without reasoning.
P2: The hidden Bite infection is a double swing (one human fewer, one wolf more) with no public trace, and it can win by round 2.
P3: The round-6 timeout gives the win to any surviving wolf, so wolves can stall.
P4: Humans have no reliable inference source. A random exposure draw decides most games, which is the lottery trap.
P5: Balance swings strongly with player count.
P6: Five hidden elements exceed the limit of 3 (bites counters and private Charm feedback are extra).
P7: Edge cases are unstated: Mauling a wolf, death versus infection order, self-targeting.
P8: Day lynches of innocents are blind coin flips, so passive, blending wolves win about half the time against humans who cannot reason from anything.

changes.what: Replace the random exposure and the blind lynch with a Trial. The day's unique top vote-getter has their role revealed publicly and truthfully. A wolf is killed. A human is publicly cleared but takes 1 wound from the mob.
changes.why: Humans get a deterministic, public inference source that good voting exploits. Mis-accusations still cost something: the cleared human becomes easy to kill. Vote records then become evidence, because whoever pushed a cleared human is suspect.

changes.what: Remove the random exposure draw entirely. There are no random draws after setup.
changes.why: The outcome is no longer decided by whether a draw landed on a wolf.

changes.what: Make vote records public and run the Trial every day.
changes.why: Two wolves who bloc-vote a human get exposed. That human is revealed as cleared, so their voters (2 of whom are wolves) become the obvious suspects next day, at about 2/3 accuracy. This punishes the thoughtless bloc policy and rewards reading votes.

changes.what: Drop Bite, bites counters and infection.
changes.why: This removes the hidden double swing and one hidden element.

changes.what: Drop Charm and its private feedback; its inspection role moves into the public Trial.

Replace the wolf timeout with a ratio rule. After the Final Night (round 5), humans win if living humans are at least 2 times living wolves; otherwise wolves win. Parity at any check still wins for wolves, and 0 wolves still wins for humans.
changes.why: Passive wolves who never Maul lose: 5 humans is at least 2x2. Stalling is not a win. Wolves must make 2 kills by round 5, or 3 for an early parity win. If one wolf is found, humans need only keep 2 alive.

changes.what: Fix the game at 7 players: 2 wolves and 5 humans.
changes.why: Balance no longer swings with player count, and one size can be checked by path reasoning.

changes.what: Use one wound limit of 2 for everyone: each Maul adds 1 wound and each Salve removes 1, applied in a fixed order.
changes.why: A kill needs both wolves on one fresh target, or one wolf on an already-wounded player. Salves are then a real guessing duel against the wolves rather than a blind lottery, because wounds are public.

changes.what: State the edge cases. A Maul may target a wolf, with normal effect. No one may target themselves. Mauls apply before Salves. The death check comes after Salves. Trial wounds can kill a player who was already wounded.
changes.why: This makes the rules complete and unambiguous.

keeps: Secret wolves among humans, with wolves knowing each other.
Wound cards that kill at a threshold and Salve cards that heal them.
A silent Night in which every player hands one face-down card to another player.
A Final Night that ends the game, where human survival decides it.
Table talk with lying allowed, and team victory in which dead players still share their team's result.

recommendation.reason: The hidden-team core is rich in inference and bluffing. It needed a public, skill-driven detection source, a fair end rule and fewer hidden elements, all of which fit within the limits.

variation.name: Growl: Trial by Moonlight
variation.summary: 7 players, 2 secret wolves. Each day everyone talks at once and then votes. The top vote-getter is put on Trial and their true role is revealed. Wolves die, while innocent humans are cleared but wounded. Each silent night, wolves Maul and everyone Salves. Wolves win at parity, or if humans are fewer than twice the wolves after the Final Night (round 5). Humans win by killing both wolves or by keeping that 2:1 ratio.
variation.rules:
PARAMETERS: 7 players, 2 wolves, wound limit 2, final round 5.

TABLE STATE: round (public, starts 0); living_wolves and living_humans (computed, used only for end checks, never announced as counts); accused (public, blank or a name); winner (blank, 'Wolves' or 'Humans').

PLAYER STATE:
- is_wolf (1 or 0): known to the player and to the other wolf.
- alive (starts 1): public.
- wounds (starts 0): public.
- cleared (starts 0): public. It becomes 1 when a Trial shows the player is human.
- revealed_role: public. Blank until death or Trial, then 'Wolf' or 'Human'.
- vote_target and votes_received: public after each vote.
- night_card and night_target: private. Never revealed.
- mauls_received and salves_received: private working counters, reset each night.

SETUP:
1. Choose 2 of the 7 players uniformly at random to be wolves; the other 5 are humans.
2. Tell each player privately whether they are a Wolf or a Human. Tell each wolf who the other wolf is.

EACH ROUND (only living players act; dead players are skipped but remain on their team):
1. Morning: round increases by 1. Publicly show every player's alive, wounds, cleared and revealed_role, and name who died last night.
2. Talk: every living player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Lying is allowed, and nothing is binding.
3. Vote: at the same time, each living player names one other living player. Abstaining and self-votes are not allowed.
4. Tally: votes_received = the number of votes each player got. Publicly show every vote_target and every votes_received.
5. Trial: if exactly one player has the most votes, that player is the accused, and their role is revealed publicly. If the top count is tied, there is no Trial today.
6. If the accused is a Wolf: they die (alive = 0, revealed_role = 'Wolf').
7. If the accused is a Human: set cleared = 1 and revealed_role = 'Human', and add 1 to their wounds.
8. Day death check: any living player with wounds >= 2 dies (alive = 0), and their role is revealed publicly.
9. Count: living_wolves = living players with is_wolf = 1; living_humans = living players with is_wolf = 0.
10. Day end check: if living_wolves = 0, the Humans win. Otherwise, if living_wolves >= living_humans, the Wolves win.
11. Wolf den: every living wolf writes one short message at the same time. These messages are shown only to living wolves.
12. Night (silent, no talk): at the same time, each living player chooses one card and one other living player as its target. A human must play Salve. A wolf plays either Maul or Salve. The card goes face-down to the target. Any player, including a wolf, may be targeted. No one may target themselves.
13. Mauls: each living player's wounds += the number of Mauls they received.
14. Salves: then each living player's wounds -= the number of Salves they received, to a minimum of 0.
15. Night death check: any living player with wounds >= 2 dies (alive = 0), and their role is revealed publicly at the next Morning.
16. Count: recompute living_wolves and living_humans.
17. Night end check: if living_wolves = 0, the Humans win. Otherwise, if living_wolves >= living_humans, the Wolves win. Otherwise, if round = 5 (the Final Night), the Humans win if living_humans >= 2 x living_wolves, and the Wolves win otherwise. If no one has won, start the next round.

NEVER REVEALED: anyone's night card or target, how many Mauls or Salves a player received (only resulting wounds and deaths are public), wolf den messages, and the role of a living player who has not been tried.
variation.objective: This is a team game decided by arithmetic. The game ends at the first of these: living wolves = 0, which is a Humans win; living wolves >= living humans at a day or night check, which is a Wolves win; or the end of round 5, where Humans win if living humans >= 2 x living wolves and Wolves win otherwise. Every player, alive or dead, wins if their team wins and loses otherwise. There are no draws.
variation.expected_effect:
Thoughtless policies lose:
- Passive wolves never Maul, so 5 humans stay at least 2x2 at round 5 and they lose.
- Bloc-voting wolves get a human cleared. That human's voters then include both wolves, and reasoning humans try one of them next day at about 2/3 accuracy, which costs the wolves the game, since a lone wolf rarely makes the remaining kills. Estimate about 35% for the thoughtless bloc-and-focus wolf policy against reasoning humans.
- Random-voting humans let the wolves steer Trials onto humans. Each cleared human becomes wounded and easy to kill. Estimate about 75% wolf wins against random humans.

With good play on both sides, the expected result is near 45/55, decided by reasoning:
- Wolves split their votes and mimic human voting.
- Wolves choose between killing cleared, trusted humans and uncleared ones (which thins the suspect pool).
- Wolves sometimes Salve or wound a partner to fake innocence.
- Humans read vote records and claims, and spread Salves to guess where the double Maul lands.

Talk passes both tests. The players disagree because wolves need humans to try innocents. A human who simply follows the first confident proposal can be led by a wolf into a Trial on a human, which wounds a teammate and wastes the day.

Talk is simultaneous, so no one can just echo the first speaker. There is no endgame unraveling, because the game ends on elimination, parity or a ratio, not on a highest total.

balanced.evidence:
Win paths. Humans win if living_wolves = 0, or if round 8 is reached with living_wolves < living_humans (wolves_won = 0). Wolves win only by reaching living_wolves >= living_humans. The single wolf has two tools. (a) Infection: 3 net Bites on one human, with bite_limit = 3. (b) Using its one vote to push humans to their deaths, which needs wound_limit = 2. The wolf has no kill of its own.

Test the passive human policy (call it P):
- Every living human names the player to their left, so each player gets 1 vote and the top count is tied.
- At night, Salve whoever is wounded.
- Charm anyone who claims to have been bitten.

Round by round under P, 5 players (1 wolf, 4 humans):
- Wolf votes along: everyone has 1 vote, a tie, nobody is wounded.
- Wolf deviates and votes X, giving X 2 votes as the unique top: X goes to 1 wound and stays alive, because the death check needs 2. That night some human Salves X, so X is back to 0. Net effect 0.
- A human can only die after two wounds with no Salve between them. Under P that never happens. The exception is the wolf itself, which no human Salves.
- Infection: the wolf Bites V each night. V sees their own bites rise and claims it in talk. The wolf can also make a false claim to spread the Charms. That costs at most 2 Charms plus 1 Salve, which is 3 cards, against 4 human cards available in 5p and 6 in 7p.
- Net bites on V never reach 3. The wolf, acting alone, can at best keep 1 bite on V for a night.

Result of P against every wolf line:
| Wolf line | Outcome |
|---|---|
| vote along | 1v4 at round 8, Humans WIN |
| deviate vote | target salved, 1v4, Humans WIN |
| bite + false claim | charmed, 1v4, Humans WIN |
| random play | Humans WIN |

P never loses. It is a thoughtless stall that needs no inference and has a strictly safe outcome. Seat edge: the single wolf seat, with probability 1/n of being drawn, has close to 0% win rate under competent human play. If humans play randomly, accidental unsalved double-wounds can occasionally give the wolf parity, but the wolf's chances still stay far below 50%. The design's stated tension, infection versus lynching, is not borne out by the numbers. The game is described as a social-deduction contest, but by its arithmetic it is a human stall.

playable.evidence:
Limits are within bounds:
- steps_per_round 14 (cap 20)
- choice steps: Talk, Accusation, Night target, Night card = 4 (cap 4)
- attributes: 3 params + 4 table + 9 player = 16 (cap 20)
- hidden_elements 2, random_draws 0, rounds 8
- no board, clock or trading

Talk is simultaneous and placed correctly, since the wolf and the humans disagree.

Gaps in the rules:
(1) It is not stated whether vote_target or votes_received are shown after the tally. Voting patterns are the only possible clue to the wolf, so a model cannot know what it learns.
(2) It is not stated whether night targets or cards are ever revealed.
(3) There is no rule saying whether a player learns that their bites went up. 'Visible to its owner' implies they can read it, but the timing is not specified.
(4) Steps 7 and 8 are separate polls, so a player commits to a target before choosing a card. The text does not say whether the target can be left unused.

Fixed-length check. In this team game, the safe option (stall: tied votes plus Salve) wins every late round for humans. Nothing a wolf does after round 1 changes that. By the brief's own criterion, a fixed-length game where the safe line wins every late round fails.

reasoning_over_luck.evidence:
Luck: the only random element is the wolf assignment. With good play, humans adopt P and win every game regardless of who the wolf is. The result is therefore decided neither by luck nor by reasoning, but by a fixed safe strategy.

Inference: there is almost nothing to infer.
- The wolf's night target is hidden.
- Votes may be hidden (see playable).
- A bitten human learns only that some wolf targeted them, not which one.
- Lynching to find the wolf is a 1/(n-1) guess per execution. Each execution takes 2 rounds and gives the wolf parity progress whenever it hits a human.

Rational humans therefore never investigate. A strong reasoner and a weak one both choose 'stall and heal' and get the same result. A reasoning wolf has no lever that beats it, so skilled play is not favoured.

required_changes: Remove the timer win for humans. If round = max_rounds with a wolf still alive, the wolves win, or the result is scored on parity progress. Humans must then actually find and kill the wolf.
Give the wolves a direct kill. For example, a wolf Bite also adds 1 wound to its target, or there is a separate wolf kill each night. A Salve should cancel at most one such wound.

Limit Salves so that stalling is impossible. Options: each player may Salve at most twice per game, or a Salve cannot remove a wound gained in that same round's vote, or wound_limit = 1 for the day vote.
Use 2 wolves for 6-7 players, or lower bite_limit to 2, and recompute so that the wolf team's win rate under good play on both sides is roughly 35-55%.

Add a source of inference and state its visibility. Publish each round's vote tally and each player's vote_target. Optionally tell a Charm sender whether their target had bites > 0, so that Charm claims can be checked.
State explicitly when a player sees their own bites change, and whether night targets or cards are ever revealed.

balanced.evidence:
**Win thresholds (6 players: 2 wolves, 4 humans).** The wolves win as soon as living_humans <= living_wolves. That means the wolves need to remove only 2 humans (4 -> 2) before the humans find both wolves.

**Thoughtless wolf policy W:** both wolves always vote for the same human, and at night both play Maul on the same human (2 wounds = wound_limit, so the target dies).

**Day 1.** Humans have zero information: there has been no exposure and no Charm yet. A human picking blindly among 5 others has P(wolf) = 2/5 = 0.40. The wolves' 2 bloc votes also split or decide the human votes. Outcomes:
- Human lynched (about 0.45): 2v3. Night kill: 2v2, wolves win.
- Tie (about 0.15): 2v4, then the night kill makes 2v3.
- Wolf lynched (about 0.40).

**Can Salve stop the kill?** Each non-target human salves one of 4 others, so each hits the target with probability about 1/4. With 2 helpers in a 2v3 position, P(at least one save) = 1 - (3/4)^2 = 0.44. The target cannot salve itself.

**Exposure.** The random exposure reveals a mauling wolf with probability W/N, about 1/3, per night.

**Rough path sum, 6 players.** P(humans win) ≈ 0.40 x 0.6 (find the second wolf, helped by the 1/3 exposure) + 0.60 x [0.44 x 0.33 x 0.5 + tie branch about 0.05] ≈ 0.24 + 0.07 ≈ 0.31. So policy W, which never adapts, wins about 70% for the wolves.

**Bite is a stronger, still thoughtless policy.** Two wolves biting the same human X reach bites 2 on night 1. One more bite on night 2 gives bites 3, and X is infected. That is a swing of -1 human and +1 wolf with no public trace: no wound, no death, no revealed role. From 2v4 with no lynch, this alone gives 3v3 and the wolves win at step 17 of round 2. Only a Charm aimed at X by another human prevents it, and blind Charm hit rate is about 1/4 per human.

**Round-6 rule.** Any surviving wolf wins at round 6, which adds a further wolf-only tiebreak.

**Payoff table (team result).**
| Ending | wolf | human |
|---|---|---|
| wolves_won = 1 | 1 | 0 |
| wolves_won = 0 | 0 | 1 |

The wolves' bloc-vote plus focus-fire (or focus-bite) policy wins most games without any reasoning.

**7 players** (2v5, 3 human losses allowed) is closer, about 45/55. So the balance also swings strongly with player count. Seat order gives no edge, because all choices are simultaneous. The asymmetry lies entirely in information (wolves know everything relevant) and in the win conditions.

playable.evidence:
**Within limits:** 18 steps per round (<= 20). 4 choice steps (talk, vote, den, night) (<= 4). About 16-19 attributes (<= 20). 1 random draw per round (the exposure; the wolf choice is setup only). 6 rounds (<= 40).

**Talk is well placed:** it is simultaneous and placed where wolves and humans disagree.

**Hidden elements exceed the limit of 3.** The game actually hides five independent kinds of information:
1. Each player's is_wolf.
2. Each player's bites, private per owner.
3. Each player's night_card and night_target, except the exposed one.
4. The wolf-den private channel.
5. Per-player private Charm feedback.

The infection notice is also a private message to the new wolf and to all wolves. The stated 'hidden_elements: 3' undercounts.

**Minor ambiguities:**
- Whether a wolf may target another wolf with Maul is not stated (presumably yes).
- Whether a newly infected wolf joins the den in the same night is unclear. Step 15 comes after step 8, so it is presumably the next night.
- Whether a player at wounds 2 who is also at bites 3 dies as a human is resolved by step order (death before infection) but is not stated.

The rules are otherwise finite and arithmetic.

reasoning_over_luck.evidence:
**What humans can infer:**
- **Charm feedback** says 'had bites' only for bitten humans. A wolf can never have bites, so 'no bites' is consistent with both wolf and unbitten human. The positive signal only clears a human and never identifies a wolf.
- **Exposure** is the only hard evidence of a wolf. It fires with probability 2/N per night (1/3 at 6 players, 2/7 at 7). It is decided entirely by the random draw.
- **Day 1** lynch is a blind 2/5 guess.
- **Salve** saves are blind 1/4 guesses.

**Sensitivity to luck (6 players).** The human win rate is about 0.31 overall. Conditioned on luck, it is about 0.65 if a wolf is exposed on night 1 and about 0.15 if not. Most of the human outcome is set by the exposure draw and the day-1 coin flip, not by reasoning.

**Both sides playing well.** Wolves bloc-vote and focus-fire; humans vote blindly and act on exposures. The result is then mostly 'did the random exposure land on a wolf'.

**Wolf decisions** do carry real reasoning: Maul versus Bite versus a disguising Salve under exposure risk. But the human side, which needs to infer, has almost nothing reliable to infer from. Vote patterns help only marginally, because wolves can blend in with a bloc. A strong human reasoner is not clearly favoured over a random voter.

required_changes: Give humans an inference source that good play can exploit, not a random draw. For example: Charm reports 'your target is a Wolf / is not a Wolf' (or 'played Bite or Maul last night: yes/no'), or replace the random exposure with a vote-chosen inspection. Keep at most 1 random draw per round, but do not make it the main way wolves are found.

Rebalance the kill and infection economy. Raise wound_limit to 3 or allow at most one Maul per night in total. Make infection need bites >= 3 from at least 2 different nights and reveal publicly that 'someone was infected', so Bite is not a hidden double swing that wins 6-player games by round 2.

Remove the 'any wolf alive at round 6 = wolves win' timeout. Either make the game end only on a parity or elimination condition, or raise max_rounds and give humans the win if they reach the last round with living_humans >= 2 x living_wolves.

Scale the wolf count with players (1 wolf at 6 players, 2 at 7, or a fixed 7 players), and show by path calculation that the always-bloc-vote, always-focus-Maul or focus-Bite wolf policy wins no more than about 55%.

Cut hidden elements to 3. For example: drop the per-player bites counter and infection (or make bites public), and fold the Charm feedback into the inspection mechanic. Keep roles, night actions and the wolf den as the three.
State explicitly: whether a wolf may Maul another wolf; that a newly infected wolf joins the den from the next night; and that death (step 14) is checked before infection (step 15).

balanced.evidence:
WOLF NIGHT CARD (the only real card choice in the game). A wolf picks Maul or Salve and a target. Humans can only Salve, so a wolf's wounds can never rise except from its own partner. Night cards and targets are never revealed, and only net wounds are public. A wolf's Salve therefore has no hidden-information value: no one ever sees which card a wolf played.

Table: change in the target's net wounds from one wolf's card, given the s Salves the target gets from others (min 0):

| Target | Maul, s=0 | Maul, s=1 | Maul, s>=2 | Salve |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Human at 0 wounds | +1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Human at 1 wound | +1, dies at 2 | 0 | -1 | -1 |
| Wolf partner | +1 (self-harm, never chosen) | | | 0 |

Against every human salve profile, Maul on a human leaves that human with wounds greater than or equal to those under Salve. So a living-human count that is lower or equal can only favour the wolves. Wolf Salve on a human can only remove a wound from an enemy. It is never better in any cell, and it is strictly worse whenever the target gets fewer salves than its wounds plus 1.

WINNER RULE: compare the thoughtless policy 'both wolves always Maul the same uncleared human' with any policy that ever plays Salve. For every combination of human votes and salves, the Maul policy produces at least as many dead humans by Round 5. The wolf win tests (wolves >= humans, or humans < 2 x wolves at Final Night) are monotone in dead humans. So the Maul policy never wins less often. The Maul/Salve choice is dominated and decorative, which is exactly the 'option better whatever the opponent does' failure. The same 2 kills can come from night mauls, from two wrong trials on the same human, or from a mix. Human night play is a pure target guess (Salve forced).

Rough strength check: 5 humans vs 2 wolves. With no deaths, Final Night gives 5 >= 4, so humans win. If wolves stay hidden they need only 2 dead humans in 5 rounds. A random-salve night kill on an uncleared 0-wound human succeeds with probability (5/6)^4 ≈ 0.48, and higher when humans concentrate salves on cleared or wounded players. If one wolf is caught, the surviving wolf needs humans <= 1, i.e. about 4 kills, which is nearly impossible. Both sides can win and seat order is irrelevant (simultaneous choices). The balance failure is the dominated card choice.

playable.evidence:
Limits:
- steps_per_round: 17 (<= 20).
- choice steps: 4, namely talk, vote, wolf den and night (<= 4).
- attributes: 16 by my count, against the designer's stated 15. Table: round, living_wolves, living_humans, accused, winner = 5. Player: is_wolf, alive, wounds, cleared, revealed_role, vote_target, votes_received, night_card, night_target, mauls_received, salves_received = 11. Still <= 20.
- hidden elements: roles, night cards/targets and den messages = 3 (<= 3).
- random draws per round: 0; the only draw is at setup.
- rounds: 5.

The game is finite (Final Night at round 5) and decided entirely by arithmetic on alive and is_wolf counts.

Edge cases are covered:
- a tie means no Trial;
- a re-accused cleared human gains a wound and can die at 2;
- a lone wolf still has a den step;
- no self-targeting;
- death checks come after the salves.

No board, clock or judge is needed. Talk is simultaneous and fits: teams conflict, roles are hidden, and following a proposal can cost humans (wolves lie). The private wolf den is supported by private_channel. The night is a simultaneous poll.

Minor note: living_wolves/humans are 'never announced', but anyone can derive them from public revealed roles and the known wolf count of 2. This is harmless.

reasoning_over_luck.evidence:
Chance enters through the random role deal and through the night, which is a simultaneous guessing game: 4 eligible human salvers against a hidden wolf target. Under mixed play the per-night kill chance sits around 0.4-0.6.

The winner is not set by the deal. It turns mainly on whether humans catch a wolf by day. The day offers real inference:
- public vote records, since wolves piling 2 votes on a human who is revealed Human become suspects;
- simultaneous claims in talk;
- public wound rises, which mark a player as almost certainly human, because wolves would have to maul their partner to fake it.

There are ways to act on that inference: a coordinated 5-vote plurality kills a wolf outright, and salves can be concentrated on players known to be human.

With good play on both sides, the outcome depends on wolf deception against human deduction plus a moderate night-guessing component. I estimate chance at about 35-45% of the result, not a deal-only outcome. A reasoning team is clearly favoured over one that votes and salves at random.

required_changes: Make the wolf's night card a real decision. Replace the human's forced Salve with a choice between Salve (as now) and Watch. Watch privately tells the watcher which card their target played that night (Maul or Salve). A wolf that Mauls can then be exposed by a watcher, while a wolf that Salves looks innocent and gives up a kill. Maul is no longer weakly dominant. Keep hidden elements at 3 by treating Watch results as part of the hidden night-card element, and keep choice steps at 4 by resolving Watch inside the existing Night step.

Alternatively, if Watch is not added, remove the Maul/Salve choice entirely so wolves always Maul. Then add a different trade-off, such as each wolf having at most 3 Mauls for the whole game, which is a public-safe private counter, so that the wolves face a real allocation decision.

After the change, re-check the Final Night threshold (humans >= 2 x wolves). Confirm with a worked table that hidden wolves need about 2 kills and that humans catching one wolf in 5 days remains roughly even.
